Revenue consensus differs by source: Benzinga $88.6M, StockAnalysis $85.91M, MarketBeat $85.7M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/IBTA/earnings-forecasts). Non-GAAP EPS is disputed ($0.38 Benzinga, $0.13 Earnings Whispers), so I sized against revenue and the company guide only. Against Q4 2025 revenue of $88.5M that is roughly $92-94M (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-3-ibotta-inc-stock/).
positioning_check: Short interest (FINRA, via equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/ibta/shortinterest): 2,765,604 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, down 438,019 from 3,203,623 on 09-30, with 9.44 days to cover (15.49 on 09-30). Against 23.17M total shares (20.15M Class A plus 3.02M Class B at 2026-07-31 per the 10-Q) that is about 12% of shares outstanding; free float is smaller, so it is probably a mid-to-high-teens % of float. The short is crowded and was covering into October. Equibles models about 2.65M for 10-30 (estimate, not FINRA). Skew: +12.69 vol points (25d put IV minus 25d call IV), so downside is paid. ATM IV 132.9%, event-implied move 23.05%, put/call OI 0.74 but total OI only 151 contracts, and the ATM spread is 27% of mid, so the option read is thin. The stock trades at its 52-week high (+157% off the low) and above every sell-side target found: consensus 'Reduce/Hold', average target $34.83-36.14 (MarketBeat/StockAnalysis, August 2026).

findings.finding: Ibotta has beaten the TOP of its own revenue guide in each of the last three quarters: Q4 2025 $88.5M against an $80-85M guide (+$3.5M), Q1 2026 $82.5M against $78-82M (+$0.5M), and Q2 2026 $88.9M against $82-86M (+$2.9M). The same habit applied to the Q3 guide of $86-90M points to about $90-93M, against a consensus of $85.7-88.6M. The one known Q3 headwind, the Walmart Deals event moving from July into Q2 (worth 2-3 points of Q2 growth), was already built into the Q3 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 beat (2026-02-25) +28.54%; Q1 2026 beat at the top of the guide (2026-05-06) -0.59%; Q2 2026 beat plus a Q3 guide above consensus and the 7-Eleven deal (2026-08-03) +51.91%. A beat alone has been bought only when the guide also moved; the Q1 beat with a flat guide went nowhere.
findings.why_not_priced: The low end of consensus ($85.7-85.9M) still sits below the guide midpoint, so some estimate sources have not caught up with the company's habit of beating. But the stock has doubled since August, which is what it would look like if the buy-side had priced a beat, so this is at best partly unpriced.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 beats from separate company releases: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260225755258/en/Ibotta-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001538379/000162828026031279/earningsrelease33126.htm. Instacart's Q3 (a separate finding below) is consistent with that publisher's order flow growing.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide is the line this stock trades on. Management's own marker is 'exit 2026 with mid-single digit year-over-year growth', which implies about $92-94M against Q4 2025's $88.5M. Since that was said, three new third-party publishers have been added or are ramping: Uber (live end of Q2, 'ramp in coming months'), Giant Eagle (live after the quarter) and 7-Eleven (exclusive CPG-offer provider for 11,500 stores and 100M+ loyalty members, live 'in the fall' per an Ibotta spokesperson; the CEO declined to size it and said it would inform 2027 commentary).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide decided both big moves: the Q2 release raised Q3 above consensus (rev midpoint $88M vs $85.86M, EBITDA $13M vs $11.38M per Barchart) and the stock rose 51.9%; the Q1 release guided Q2 to -2% y/y and the stock moved -0.6%. In 2025, guides below expectations produced -23.7% (Nov 2025) and -30.3% (Aug 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody outside the company has sized 7-Eleven, Uber or Giant Eagle, and the management marker was given before those ramps. If the market had priced a raised Q4 and a first 2027 comment, sell-side targets would have moved above $49. They still sit at $35-45 (Needham $45 the highest found), so the sell-side is not there, although the tape (+100%) suggests the buy-side is.
findings.independence: 7-Eleven go-live timing comes from trade press quoting an Ibotta spokesperson: https://www.retail-insight-network.com/newsletters/ibotta-exclusive-cpg-offers-provider-7-eleven. Partner list in the Q2 release (same document as the bar).

findings.finding: The bar is high: IBTA closed $24.58 before the Q2 print and about $49.3 on 2026-11-02 (+100%), +19.7% over 20 days, at its 52-week high. That includes an unexplained +10.15% on 2026-10-15 with no company release that day. Sell-side consensus is Reduce/Hold with an average target of $34.83-36.14, and the option skew pays +12.7 vol points for downside. The downside is limited by a crowded short that is covering (2.77M shares, about 12% of shares outstanding, down 438k into 10-15).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's last seven reactions split 3 up and 4 down, median |move| 28.5%. The two prints that followed big run-ups in 2025 (Feb 2025 -46.1%, Aug 2025 -30.3%) fell hard. The Q2 2026 print came off a depressed base ($24.58) and rose 51.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is mostly priced by construction; the skew already says it. It is filed because it sets the reaction bar for every other finding: with the stock at double its pre-Q2 level, an in-line beat-and-hold guide is not enough.
findings.independence: Sell-side targets: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/ibotta-nyseibta-shares-gap-up-after-analyst-upgrade-2026-08-04/ . Short interest (works against this finding): https://equibles.com/stocks/ibta/shortinterest . Skew from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Steady insider selling into the run: about 27 Form 4s and 20 Form 144s since 2026-08-01, including CEO Bryan Leach exercising and selling about 15k shares at $41.36-41.57 on 10-05/06, the CTO selling at $49.91-49.97 on 10-21/22, and 11 more Form 144 notices filed 10-19 to 10-30. Leach's and the CTO's sales are flagged as Rule 10b5-1 plan trades. An aggregator puts the 12-month total at $42.7M across 5 insiders.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to insider sales on this name. MarketBeat headlined a gap down after insider selling on 2026-08-18, size not established.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced and routine (10b5-1 option exercises). It is filed because the 144 cluster in the last two weeks before the print is the only insider signal there is, and it is not a buy.

findings.finding: The buyback is large relative to the float. H1 2026 repurchases were 2,659,708 shares ($68.4M), about 11% of the 23.2M shares outstanding; Q2 alone was 711k shares at $32.33. $67.3M remains on the $400M authorization, cash is $148.2M and the revolver is undrawn. Management raised full-year FCF conversion to about 70% of adjusted EBITDA. The company has topped up the authorization by $100M before, so another increase, or a Q3 repurchase count, at this print would shrink the float further into a crowded short.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Earlier $100M authorization increases were announced (silicon.co.uk press-release copies) without a measured standalone reaction. Prints with buyback news (Q4 2025, Q2 2026) rose, but alongside a beat and a guide raise.
findings.why_not_priced: The remaining $67.3M buys only about 1.4M shares at $49, so a fresh authorization is the incremental news, and it is not certain. If the market had priced a re-up, the short would not still be about 12% of shares outstanding.
findings.independence: Earlier authorization increase: https://www.silicon.co.uk/press-release/ibotta-announces-a-100-million-increase-to-its-share-repurchase-program . Q2 repurchase in the release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001538379/000162828026051867/earningsrelease63026.htm

findings.finding: Counterparty read (Instacart is an IPN publisher, reported 2026-10-29, after Ibotta last spoke): Q3 GTV $10.53B, +15% y/y, at the top of its $10.3-10.55B guide; orders 91.4M, +10%; advertising and other revenue +23%. The release does not mention Ibotta or CPG coupons.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured; publisher launches (DoorDash, Instacart) drove 2025-26 redeemer growth per the company.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy: Ibotta's take on Instacart orders is undisclosed and Instacart is one of several publishers. It is filed small. The positive read is mostly overshadowed in coverage by the DoorDash deal announced alongside it.
findings.independence: Instacart's own Q3 release PDF: https://s25.q4cdn.com/251036341/files/doc_financials/2026/q3/CART-Q3-26-Earnings-Results-and-DoorDash-Acquisition-Press-Release.pdf (same results).

findings.finding: DoorDash agreed on 2026-10-29 to acquire Instacart (about $17B, $65/share), which would combine two of Ibotta's named IPN publishers under one owner with its own advertising tools. Closing is expected end-2027 or 1H 2028, so nothing changes commercially in the window, but analysts are likely to ask about publisher concentration on the 11-02 call. IBTA moved -0.59% on 10-23 (first reports) and +2.00% on 10-29 (announcement).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: IBTA barely moved on the deal days (-0.59% 10-23, +2.00% 10-29).
findings.why_not_priced: The stock's flat reaction suggests the market sees no near-term effect. A sharp answer on the call either way (renewal terms, exclusivity) is the only way it enters the window.

findings.finding: Board change 2026-09-22: director Thomas Lehrman resigned 'effective immediately', with no disagreement stated; Tony Weisman was appointed to the board and the Audit Committee. Separately, the securities class action was dismissed in full on 2026-08-03, without prejudice, with leave to file a second amended complaint by 2026-08-31. Whether that complaint was filed is unverified.
findings.why_not_priced: Already public and immaterial to the print; filed for completeness.
findings.independence: Class action dismissal in the Q2 10-Q subsequent events: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001538379/000162828026052575/ibta-20260630.htm

baseline_tension: My findings net slightly positive (beat habit, buyback, new publishers), which cuts against the +12.7 put skew and a +100% run since the last print. The crowded, covering short is the reason the negative positioning finding stays small.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat-habit finding went from +1.5 to +1.0, because the Q1 2026 beat with a flat guide moved -0.6%.
Lesson 7 (positioning): the high-bar finding went from -1.5 to -1.0. It agrees with the skew, but short interest is about 12% of shares outstanding, 9.4 days to cover, and covering.
Lesson 5 (a narrow proxy): the Instacart counterparty read went from +0.5 to +0.3, because Ibotta's exposure to it is undisclosed.
Lesson 3/6 (window): the DoorDash-Instacart finding went from -0.3 to -0.2, because its commercial effect lands after the window; the closing itself is filed in outside_window.
Left standing: the guidance finding (+1.0, wide band), the buyback (+0.8), insider selling (-0.3), board/legal (0); abs_move 25 and p_up 51 unchanged.
